findings.description: The EARS text is silent on what happens when a position's Est. Tax Rate hasn't been computed yet (symbol absent from `effective_rates`, a 'degraded' tax estimate) — it only states the Net Unrealized formula assuming a rate exists. This forces all three A runs to invent divergent, mutually incompatible handling: A1 wraps the formula in `IFERROR(...,"")` to render blank on error; A2 models the rate as `Option<i32>` and substitutes a literal `"—"` placeholder in both the rate cell and a `="—"` net-formula; A3 assumes no defensive handling at all, letting a native Sheets `#VALUE!`/blank-as-zero surface. None of the three matches the real mechanism, which all three B runs independently and consistently reconstruct: `render_positions` writes the Est. Tax Rate cell as an engine VALUE that is an EMPTY STRING (`eff_rate.map(fmt_ppm).unwrap_or_default()`) and deliberately leaves the post-tax formulas UNCHANGED (`=G{r}*H{r}`, `=G{r}*(1-H{r})`); Sheets coerces the blank H to 0, so 'Est. Unrealized Tax (est)' silently becomes 0 and 'Net Unrealized (est)' silently becomes numerically IDENTICAL to the pre-tax 'Unrealized P&L' — a specific, load-bearing degrade contract the spec text never states, and that no A implementation reproduced. This is the strongest finding: a real sub-decision the spec leaves open (surfacing as 3-way A disagreement) whose actual resolution in code (surfacing as tight B agreement) is a form none of the A guesses anticipated.

The code renders a THIRD figure the spec text never names: 'Est. Unrealized Tax (est)' = Unrealized P&L × Est. Tax Rate, formula `=G{r}*H{r}`, sitting in its own header column immediately next to 'Net Unrealized (est)'. The spec's only textual hook for a second post-tax column is the plural 'the post-tax columns shall be labelled estimates' — it never defines what that second column is or its formula. All three B runs independently pinned this exact column/formula/header ('Est. Unrealized Tax (est)'); none of the three A sketches invented it — each A implementation produces only the two things the spec literally names (pre-tax Unrealized P&L, and the Net Unrealized formula). Clean code-side surplus: a whole extra formula-bearing column the spec text does not force.

The spec says only that Est. Tax Rate is 'written by tax' — no representation or encoding is specified. The real code pins an exact, load-bearing string format via `fmt_ppm`: a percent-suffixed string with EXACTLY 4 fractional digits (e.g. `Ppm(150_000)` → `"15.0000%"`), and a dedicated test (`est_tax_rate_cell_is_numeric_percent_the_posttax_formulas_can_multiply`) exists solely to pin that this string must be written as a plain `userEnteredValue` (never a forced/string value) so Sheets coerces it to the numeric fraction (e.g. 0.20) that `=G*H`/`=G*(1-H)` require to evaluate numerically rather than to 0/text. All three B runs reconstruct this encoding contract in detail. None of the three A runs anticipated it: A1 and A3 both assumed a plain 0.0–1.0 float fraction with no format contract; A2 modeled the rate as `Option<i32>` basis points converted to a decimal only at formula-emission time. Since the spec never constrains representation, this is pure code-side surplus, not a spec-forced A-side gap.

A dedicated test (`per_row_formulas_reference_their_own_row_beneath_frozen_header`) and accompanying documentation pin a row-safety invariant the spec text never states: every per-row Positions formula (Market Value, Unrealized P&L, and by extension the post-tax formulas built on them) must reference ONLY its own row's cell numbers — the test explicitly asserts no OTHER data row's `E{other}`/`B{other}` etc. address ever appears in a row's formula string, guarding against row-insertion/reorder mis-pairing. All three B runs captured this as an explicit 'unwanted behavior' clause; nothing in the EARS text hints at it. Secondary in importance relative to findings 1–3 since it's a correctness guarantee rather than a labeled requirement gap.

`render_positions` returns `Err(ViewError::DuplicateSymbolRow(symbol))` if `Snapshot.positions` ever yields two rows for one symbol — a defensive guard all three B runs reconstructed as an 'unwanted behavior' EARS clause, though the source comments and all three B runs themselves flag it as structurally unreachable via the real `Map<Symbol,_>` source. Least material of the findings: it's a whole-tab defensive invariant, not specific to the pre/post-tax math SHEET-FORMULA-003 governs, and is self-described as non-normative even by the code.

notes: Strong A-side agreement on the core architectural reading: sheets-view emits live spreadsheet formulas (not Rust-computed values) for Unrealized P&L and Net Unrealized, consistent with 'sheets-view owns no accounting or tax math' and the GOOGLEFINANCE-oracle context — this matches the real code exactly (Cell::Formula for both). Where the three A runs genuinely diverge (beyond the degraded-rate handling captured as finding 1): (a) Est. Tax Rate representation — A1/A3 assume a plain 0.0-1.0 float, A2 alone assumes Option<i32> basis points; (b) whether the 'estimate' label applies only to Net Unrealized (A1) or also to Est. Tax Rate's own header (A2, A3) — the real code labels neither the rate column nor gives it an '(est)' suffix, so A1 is closer here but not for a spec-traceable reason; (c) whether out-of-range rates get clamped (A2) or passed through unclamped (A1, A3). None of these three secondary splits trace to spec text either way (pure invented-assumption disagreement), so I did not report them as standalone drift findings, only as the source of the 'medium' aAgreement rating. B-side agreement is high: B1/B2/B3 converge almost verbatim on column set, exact formula strings, DATA_START_ROW=2, the percent-format encoding contract, the degrade-to-empty-string mechanism and its downstream effect on the post-tax formulas, the row-self-reference invariant, and the DuplicateSymbolRow clause — the only cosmetic differences are wording/EARS-clause-numbering, not substance.
